'''David John Kennedy''' (born November 5, 1989) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Trotamundos de Carabobo]] of the [[Superliga Profesional de Baloncesto]] (SPB). He played [[college basketball]] for [[St. John's University (New York City)|St. John's University]].

==High school career==
Kennedy attended [[Schenley High School]] in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. As a senior in 2006–07, he averaged 17.7 points, 7.5 rebounds, 4.5 assists and 2.0 blocks per game. In helping the Spartans to a 29–3 record and the 2007 PIAA AAAA State championship, he earned a first team all-state selection, a first team all-city selection and a two-time Pittsburgh Post-Gazette "Fabulous Five" selection.<ref name=bio>{{cite web | url=http://www.redstormsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/dj_kennedy_318186.html | title=D.J. Kennedy Bio | work=redstormsports.com | access-date=April 22, 2014 | archive-date=May 21, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140521150914/http://www.redstormsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/dj_kennedy_318186.html | url-status=dead }}</ref>

==College career==
In his freshman season at [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]], Kennedy finished second on the squad with 37 steals, including 20 in [[Big East Conference|BIG EAST]] play. In 30 games (29 starts), he averaged 7.8 points, 5.8 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 1.2 steals per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name=stats>{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/dj-kennedy-1.html | title=D.J. Kennedy Stats | work=Sports-Reference.com | access-date=April 22, 2014}}</ref>

In his sophomore season, he was one of only two Red Storm players to start and play in each of the squad's 34 games. In those 34 games, he averaged 13.0 points, 6.6 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.5 steals in 34.6 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

In his junior season, he earned a first team All-Met selection by the Metropolitan Basketball Writers Association (MBWA). In 33 games (31 starts), he averaged 15.1 points, 6.1 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 1.2 steals in 31.4 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

In his senior season, he scored a total of 333 points to finish his college career at St. John's as the school's 12 all-time leading scorer with 1,504 total points, as well as finish 11th all-time in rebounds (781) and sixth all-time in steals (183). In 32 games, he averaged 10.4 points, 5.6 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.8 steals in 28.7 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

==Professional career==

===2011–12 season===
Kennedy went undrafted in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. In November 2011, he was acquired by the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/erie/bayhawks_announce_returning_pl_2011_11_02.html | archive-url=https://archive.today/20140422143327/http://www.nba.com/dleague/erie/bayhawks_announce_returning_pl_2011_11_02.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=April 22, 2014 | title=BayHawks Announce Returning Players, Training Camp Invites | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=November 2, 2011 | access-date=April 22, 2014 }}</ref>

On April 21, 2012, he signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] for the rest of the 2011–12 season.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/kennedy_120421.html | title=Cavaliers Sign D.J. Kennedy | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=April 21, 2012 | access-date=April 22, 2014}}</ref>

===2012–13 season===
In July 2012, Kennedy joined the Cleveland Cavaliers for the 2012 NBA Summer League. On July 25, 2012, he was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies_acquire_dj_kennedy-120725 | title=Grizzlies acquire D.J. Kennedy from Cavaliers | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=July 25, 2012 | access-date=April 22, 2014}}</ref> On September 18, 2012, he was waived by the Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-waive-dj-kennedy-120918 | title=Grizzlies waive D.J. Kennedy | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=September 18, 2012 | access-date=April 22, 2014}}</ref> Later that month, he re-signed with the Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11017 | title=Memphis Grizzlies add Michael Dunigan, Ronald Dupree, Jarrid Famous, Jerome Jordan, D.J. Kennedy to training camp | work=InsideHoops.com | date=September 29, 2012 | access-date=April 22, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140327080701/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11017 | archive-date=March 27, 2014 | url-status=dead }}</ref> On October 7, 2012, he was again waived by the Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/kennedy_famous_waived_121007 | title=Grizzlies waive Kennedy and Famous | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=October 7, 2012 | access-date=April 22, 2014}}</ref> On November 1, 2012, he was re-acquired by the Erie BayHawks.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/erie/bayhawks_add_nine__training__2012_11_01.html | title=BayHawks Add Nine to Training Camp Roster | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=November 1, 2012 | access-date=April 22, 2014 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107003516/http://www.nba.com/dleague/erie/bayhawks_add_nine__training__2012_11_01.html | archive-date=November 7, 2012 }}</ref>

On February 4, 2013, Kennedy was named to the Prospects All-Star roster for the 2013 NBA D-League All-Star Game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/2013_nba_development_league_all_star_rosters_announced_2013_02_04.html |title=2013 NBA Development League All-Star Game Rosters Announced |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |date=February 4, 2013 |access-date=April 22, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022065410/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/2013_nba_development_league_all_star_rosters_announced_2013_02_04.html |archive-date=October 22, 2013 }}</ref>

On March 5, 2013, Kennedy was traded to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/riograndevalley/VipersTRade030513.html | title=Vipers acquire Kennedy and Singletary from Erie | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=March 5, 2013 | access-date=April 22, 2014 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140522200201/http://www.nba.com/dleague/riograndevalley/VipersTRade030513.html | archive-date=May 22, 2014 }}</ref> He went on to win the 2013 NBA D-League championship with the Vipers.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13130 | title=Rio Grande Valley Vipers win 2013 D-League championship | work=InsideHoops.com | date=April 27, 2013 | access-date=April 22, 2014}}</ref>

===2013–14 season===
In July 2013, Kennedy joined the [[Miami Heat]] for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/heat/heat-announce-summer-league-information | title=HEAT Announce Summer League Information | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=July 2, 2013 | access-date=April 22, 2014}}</ref> On September 10, 2013, he signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-add-three-players-roster-expands-18/ | title=MAVERICKS ADD THREE PLAYERS; ROSTER EXPANDS TO 18 | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=September 10, 2013 | access-date=September 10, 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130927074815/http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-add-three-players-roster-expands-18/ | archive-date=September 27, 2013 | url-status=dead }}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Mavericks on October 22, 2013.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-request-waivers-balkman-ebanks-kennedy-melo/ | title=MAVERICKS REQUEST WAIVERS ON BALKMAN, EBANKS, KENNEDY AND MELO | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=October 22, 2013 | access-date=April 22, 2014 | archive-date=May 21, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140521121051/http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-request-waivers-balkman-ebanks-kennedy-melo/ | url-status=dead }}</ref>

On October 27, 2013, he signed with [[BCM Gravelines]] of France for the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/107447/gravelines-dunkerque-signs-dj-kennedy.html | title=Gravelines-Dunkerque signs DJ Kennedy | work=Sportando.com | date=October 27, 2013 | access-date=April 22, 2014}}</ref> On December 3, 2013, he parted ways with Gravelines after just 8 games.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/108833/dj-kennedy-leaves-gravelines-dunkerque.html | title=DJ Kennedy leaves Gravelines-Dunkerque | work=Sportando.com | date=December 3, 2013 | access-date=April 22, 2014}}</ref> On January 4, 2014, he signed with [[Hapoel Holon]] of Israel for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/109975/hapeol-holon-sign-dj-kennedy.html | title=Hapeol Holon sign D.J Kennedy | work=Sportando.com | date=January 4, 2014 | access-date=April 22, 2014}}</ref>

===2014–15 season===
In July 2014, Kennedy joined the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Schuster | first=Megan | url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/2014-summer-league-roster-breakdown | title=2014 Summer League Roster Breakdown | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=July 9, 2014 | access-date=September 1, 2014}}</ref> On September 1, 2014, he signed with [[BC Krasny Oktyabr|Krasny Oktyabr]] of Russia for the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/133279/krasny-oktyabr-signs-dj-kennedy.html | title=Krasny Oktyabr signs DJ Kennedy | work=Sportando.com | date=September 1, 2014 | access-date=September 1, 2014}}</ref> On November 18, 2014, he left the club after appearing in just six games.<ref>{{cite news|title=DJ Kennedy leaves Krasny Oktyabr|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/141528/dj-kennedy-leaves-krasny-oktyabr.html|access-date=November 18, 2014|date=November 18, 2014|work=Sportando.com}}</ref> On December 6, 2014, he signed with [[MHP Riesen Ludwigsburg]] of Germany for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=DJ Kennedy signs with MHP Riesen Ludwigsburg|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/143875/dj-kennedy-signs-with-mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg.html|access-date=December 6, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=December 6, 2014}}</ref>

===2015–16 season===
In July 2015, Kennedy joined the [[Houston Rockets]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]]. On August 10, 2015, he signed with [[BC Yenisey Krasnoyarsk|Yenisey Krasnoyarsk]] of Russia for the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=DJ Kennedy officially signs with Enisey Krasnoyarsk|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/172211/dj-kennedy-officially-signs-with-enisey-krasnoyarsk.html|access-date=August 10, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=August 10, 2015}}</ref> In 40 games and 38 starts, he averaged 14.9 points, 7.4 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game.<ref name="Nuggets">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-four-players-to-contracts-091516|title=Nuggets Sign Four Players to Contracts|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=September 15, 2016|access-date=September 16, 2016}}</ref>

===2016–17 season===
On September 15, 2016, Kennedy signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]],<ref name="Nuggets" /> but was waived on October 15 after appearing in one preseason game.<ref>{{cite web|author=NuggetsPR|url=https://twitter.com/NuggetsPR/status/787324175207702528|title=#Nuggets Waive Kennedy, Sampson and...|work=Twitter|date=October 15, 2016|access-date=October 15, 2016}}</ref> On November 14, he signed with [[Guangzhou Long-Lions]] of [[Chinese Basketball Association|China]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/217365/foshan-long-lions-replace-ryan-boatright-with-dj-kennedy.html|title=Foshan Long Lions replace Ryan Boatright with DJ Kennedy|work=Sportando.com|date=November 14, 2016|access-date=November 19, 2016}}</ref> Four days later, he made his debut in an 89–88 loss to [[Qingdao DoubleStar]], recording 24 points, 12 rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/China/2016/1118_7300_3514.asp|title=Regular Season Round 8: Qingdao E. – Guangzhou 89–88|work=Eurobasket.com|date=November 18, 2016|access-date=November 19, 2016}}</ref>

On March 16, 2017, Kennedy returned to his former club [[MHP Riesen Ludwigsburg]] for the rest of the [[2016–17 Basketball Bundesliga|2016–17 BBL season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=D.J. Kennedy zurück bei den MHP RIESEN!|url=https://www.mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg.de/d-j-kennedy-zurueck-bei-den-mhp-riesen/|access-date=March 16, 2017|work=mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg.de|date=March 16, 2017|language=de|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170317143621/https://www.mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg.de/d-j-kennedy-zurueck-bei-den-mhp-riesen/|archive-date=March 17, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===2017–18 season===
On August 11, 2017, Kennedy signed with Turkish club [[Karşıyaka Basket|Pınar Karşıyaka]] for the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=" D.J. KENNEDY PINAR KARŞIYAKA'DA! "|url=http://www.kskbasketbol.net/d-j-kennedy-pinar-karsiyakada/|access-date=August 11, 2017|work=kskbasketbol.net|date=August 11, 2017|language=tr}}</ref> He was the leading scorer of the [[2017–18 Basketball Champions League]] season, with 19 points per game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.championsleague.basketball/17-18/playerstats|title = Players statistics of the Basketball Champions League 2017–2018}}</ref> Karşıyaka was eliminated in the quarter-finals of the Champions League and finished tenth in the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]].

===2018–19 season===
On September 9, 2018, Kennedy signed with [[Melbourne United]] for the [[2018–19 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/melbourne-united-complete-roster-with-dj-kennedy|title=Melbourne United Complete Roster with DJ Kennedy|work=NBL.com.au|date=September 9, 2018|access-date=September 9, 2018|archive-date=March 23, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210323044710/https://nbl.com.au/news/article/melbourne-united-complete-roster-with-dj-kennedy|url-status=dead}}</ref> In March 2019, following the conclusion of the NBL season, he signed with [[Reyer Venezia]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.australiabasket.com/Australia/news/572537/Umana-Venezia-tabs-DJ-Kennedy,-ex-United|title=Umana Venezia tabs DJ Kennedy, ex United|work=australiabasket.com|date=March 22, 2019|access-date=March 26, 2019}}</ref>

===2019–20 season===
On September 25, 2019, he has signed with his former club [[Karşıyaka Basket|Pınar Karşıyaka]] for 3+6 months deal, as an injury cover for [[Tony Crocker]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.basketfaul.com/haber?haber=83444|title=DJ Kennedy Karşıyaka'ya döndü|date=September 24, 2019|website=Basketfaul|language=tr|access-date=September 25, 2019}}</ref> Kennedy averaged 9.9 points and 6.2 rebounds per game.<ref name="pinar">{{cite news |title=Pinar Karsiyaka re-signs DJ Kennedy |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/pinar-karsiyaka-re-signs-dj-kennedy/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 20, 2020 |date=July 20, 2020}}</ref>

===2020–21 season===
On July 20, 2020, Kennedy signed a two-year extension with Pınar Karşıyaka.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/pinar-karsiyaka-re-signs-dj-kennedy/|title=Pinar Karsiyaka re-signs DJ Kennedy|last=|first=|date=July 20, 2020|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 8, 2021}}</ref> He averaged 7.8 points, 5.2 rebounds, and 2.2 assists per game.<ref name="prometey" />

===2021–22 season===
On September 24, 2021, Kennedy signed with [[BC Prometey|Prometey Kamianske]] of the [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague]].<ref name="prometey">{{cite web |title=Prometey signs DJ Kennedy |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Basketball-Champions-League/news/705894/Prometey-signs-DJ-Kennedy |website=Eurobasket |access-date=September 24, 2021 |date=September 24, 2021}}</ref>

On March 9, 2022, he has signed with [[Hapoel Galil Elyon]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Israel/news/734668/DJ-Kennedy-signed-with-Hapoel-Galil-Elion|title=DJ Kennedy signed with Hapoel Galil Elion|last=|first=|date=March 9, 2022|website=|publisher=Eurobasket|language=En|access-date=March 9, 2022}}</ref>

===2022–23 season===
On July 28, 2022, he has signed with [[BC Prometey|Prometey]] of the [[Latvian-Estonian Basketball League]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/dj-kennedy-joins-prometey-again/|title=DJ Kennedy joins Prometey again|last=|first=|date=July 28, 2022|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 12, 2022 |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }}</ref>

==The Basketball Tournament==
Kennedy joined the inaugural [[Overseas Elite]] roster for [[The Basketball Tournament]] (TBT)—a single-elimination winner-take-all tournament—during the summer of 2015. Overseas Elite defeated [[Team 23]] in the [[The Basketball Tournament 2015|TBT 2015]] championship game, 67–65, to claim the $1 million prize.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://247sports.com/Bolt/Team-wins-1-million-in-winner-take-all-hoops-tournament-38521826 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150806013111/http://247sports.com/Bolt/Team-wins-1-million-in-winner-take-all-hoops-tournament-38521826 |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 6, 2015 |title=Team wins $1 million in winner-take-all hoops tournament |first=Kevin |last=Ryan |date=August 2, 2015 |access-date=August 10, 2017}}</ref> Kennedy scored 24 points in the game, and was subsequently named MVP.<ref name="thesportsquotient.com">{{cite web |url=http://thesportsquotient.com/other/2015/8/24/sq-at-the-basketball-tournaments-million-dollar-final |title=SQ At The Basketball Tournament's Million Dollar Final |first1=Dylan |last1=Turk |first2=Drew |last2=Margolis |website=thesportsquotient.com |date=August 24, 2015 |access-date=July 29, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180730110317/http://thesportsquotient.com/other/2015/8/24/sq-at-the-basketball-tournaments-million-dollar-final |archive-date=July 30, 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Overseas Elite and Kennedy repeated as champions in [[The Basketball Tournament 2016|TBT 2016]] with a 77–72 victory over Team Colorado, earning them that year's $2 million prize,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.denverpost.com/2016/08/02/team-colorado-falls-in-tbt-final-to-overseas-elite |title=Team Colorado falls in TBT final to Overseas Elite |first=Alissa |last=Noe |date=August 2, 2016 |access-date=August 10, 2017}}</ref> with Kennedy named to the All-Tournament Team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thetournament.com/news/tbt-2016-all-tournament-team |title=TBT 2016 All Tournament Team |website=thetournament.com |date=August 2016 |access-date=July 29, 2018 |archive-date=August 6, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806033000/https://www.thetournament.com/news/tbt-2016-all-tournament-team |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Kennedy and his team became three-time champions with an 86–83 win over Team Challenge ALS in [[The Basketball Tournament 2017|TBT 2017]], bringing their total winnings to $5 million. Kennedy averaged 15 points, 6.5 rebounds and 3.2 assists per game and was again named to the All-Tournament Team.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://thetournament.com/news/tbt-2017-all-tournament-team |title=TBT 2017 All-Tournament Team |website=thetournament.com |date=August 4, 2017 |access-date=August 10, 2017 |archive-date=August 6, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806065703/https://www.thetournament.com/news/tbt-2017-all-tournament-team |url-status=dead }}</ref> On August 3, 2018, Kennedy and Overseas Elite won [[The Basketball Tournament 2018|TBT 2018]], securing their fourth consecutive championship and another $2 million prize, with Kennedy being named MVP and a member of the All-Tournament Team. In [[The Basketball Tournament 2019|TBT 2019]], Kennedy and Overseas Elite advanced to the semifinals where they suffered their first-ever defeat, losing to eventual champions [[Carmen's Crew]], 71–66.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://thetournament.com/news/1-carmens-crew-71-1-overseas-elite-66 |title=#1 Carmen's Crew 71, #1 Overseas Elite 66 |website=thetournament.com |date=August 4, 2019 |access-date=August 4, 2019 |archive-date=January 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200123041911/http://www.thetournament.com/news/1-carmens-crew-71-1-overseas-elite-66 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Kennedy was again named to the All-Tournament Team.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=thetournament |number=1158956319522598912 |title=These guys were UNREAL this summer! Your #TBT2019 All-Tournament team! |date=August 7, 2019 |access-date=August 7, 2019}}</ref> Kennedy did not play for Overseas Elite during [[The Basketball Tournament 2020|TBT 2020]]; the team lost in the semifinals.

For [[The Basketball Tournament 2021|TBT 2021]], with Overseas Elite not entering the tournament, Kennedy joined [[Boeheim's Army]], a team rostered primarily with [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball]] alumni.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.si.com/college/syracuse/basketball/dj-kennedy-added-to-boeheims-army-roster |title=DJ Kennedy Joins Boeheim's Army |first=Mike |last=McAllister |website=All Syracuse FN |via=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=July 3, 2021 |accessdate=August 1, 2021}}</ref> Boeheim's Army captured the championship and $1 million prize.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/ncaabk/boeheims-army-wins-the-basketball-tournament/ar-AAMUB5n |title=Boeheim's Army Wins The Basketball Tournament |first=Mike |last=McAllister |website=All Syracuse FN |via=MSN.com |date=August 3, 2021 |accessdate=August 3, 2021}}</ref>
